prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation: the design of small molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase for destruction, from the first bifunctional PROTAC to the identification of cereblon as the target through which thalidomide-type glues act.

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as my single-part choice. The round-1 exchange did not change my reading of the science: a small molecule that brings a target and an E3 ligase together converts ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical event, and the event is catalytic, so one molecule removes many target molecules. The mechanism is defined at the level of ternary-complex structure and cooperativity, and cereblon as the thalidomide target gives the glue branch a chemical explanation that was missing for decades. The principle has been reproduced in many independent laboratories and extended to targets with no active site. The chair asked whether this can be stated as one discovery with three names. I think it can if the citation is written around the shared mechanism, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and credits three firsts: Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept and the first demonstration, Handa for cereblon as the thalidomide target. I accept that this is a statement of who established the concept, which is the standard Zou asked for, and not who made the best compounds. On timing, I weigh evidence of mechanism and reproducibility above approval status, and both are in hand. I recognise that a clinical approval would help and that the committee may not share this weighting.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the therapeutic argument is still based on trial data, and several colleagues (Linke, Zou, Aqvist) treat that as a reason to wait. Attribution is the harder problem. Ciulli's VHL ligand and ternary-complex work, Gray's contributions to degraders and the thalidomide-analogue glue work, and Sakamoto's and Kim's roles in the first PROTAC all make a three-name cut contestable, and I cannot show that Handa should outrank Ciulli by a margin the committee would accept. The configuration also joins two histories, bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, that a sceptic can count as two prizes. Finally, base editing is supported by five of eight members and has a clinical record that degraders lack. I do not treat a support count as scientific judgment, but it is a fair sign that my preference may reflect my biomedical orientation more than the committee's chemistry-wide view.

responses.point: Linke asks for a precise statement of who first showed what in B008: the PROTAC concept, cereblon as the thalidomide target, or ternary-complex design. He also notes that base editing has the same age but has already treated patients.
responses.response: That is a fair question and I will answer it directly. The PROTAC concept and the first working molecule are from Crews and Deshaies with Sakamoto and Kim in 2001. Cereblon as the thalidomide target is Handa's, and it is what explains the glue branch chemically. Ternary-complex design, cooperativity and a well-characterised E3 ligand (VHL) are mainly Ciulli's. A three-name prize therefore credits the concept and the glue mechanism and leaves the quantitative design rules to a citation caveat, and I accept that this is a judgment and not a clean boundary. On patients, I agree that base editing has clinical experience that degraders do not have, and I do not dismiss it. I still read the chemistry-gap question differently: base editing is a new use of deaminases on a CRISPR targeting scaffold, while degradation opens a new way for a small molecule to act on a protein.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that base editing is a chemist's invention built on an evolved deaminase, that Liu alone is defensible, and that Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID should be a citation caveat and not a fourth name.
responses.response: Your answer on Target-AID is persuasive on one point. The Liu-group cytosine and adenine editors preceded the independent work, and the adenine base editor needed directed evolution that nothing earlier had done. I withdraw my round-1 objection that a Liu-only prize is unclean, because the claim holds if the citation is worded around the evolved deaminase. My remaining disagreement is about weight. The Liu-only version excludes Komor and Gaudelli, who did the decisive first experiments. The three-name limit makes the same kind of cut in degradation. I would not say either attribution is cleaner than the other. I also still think the CRISPR prize makes the chemical-novelty question for B058 more demanding than for B008, and I would like it answered in the citation text and not only in the discussion.

responses.point: Zou pairs C-N coupling with base editing, and says B008 should be deferred because of eight credible names, the three-person limit and no approved PROTAC. If the committee wants a degrader prize, the case for Crews, Deshaies and Handa over Ciulli must rest on who established the concept.
responses.response: I accept your test and I think it favours my configuration: the concept and first demonstration are Crews and Deshaies, and the molecular basis of the glue mechanism is Handa. I do not claim the case against Ciulli is closed. If the committee were to find that the ternary-complex work is the defining step, my position would need to change, and I would then ask whether Ciulli replaces Handa or Deshaies. On deferring, I disagree only partly. Waiting for an approval is reasonable, but the mechanistic evidence is already independent and quantitative, and the same logic would apply to base editing, which has a shorter clinical record. I also have not heard the argument that C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize, so I keep it only as a clean-attribution alternative, not a first choice.

responses.point: Aili argues that maturity favours ionizable lipid nanoparticles over B008, because LNP medicines are used on billions of people while no PROTAC is approved, and that Cullis, Hope and Madden's work is chemistry in substance.
responses.response: The maturity argument is correct as a matter of use, and I do not dispute it. My difficulty is with what the use proves about the discovery. The distinction I would want the committee to draw is between the ionizable-lipid and formulation principle, which you attribute to Cullis, Hope and Madden, and the later lipid libraries and industrial optimisation of the lipids actually in approved products, which came from other groups. Your own statement and Sparr's both concede that attribution is weak, and the committee cannot verify who first showed that pKa tuning is what drives endosomal release. The Medicine prize in 2023 also leaves less room for a delivery vehicle for mRNA. I rank B064 low for that reason and not because I doubt the chemistry.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli (or Deshaies) should hold the third name, and whether the committee would accept an explicit caveat for Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim.
Whether the committee reads recognition before any PROTAC approval as premature, and whether an approval within a year would change its view.
Whether bifunctional PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues can be sustained as one achievement in a single citation.
How the committee weighs the 2020 CRISPR prize against base editing and the 2010 prize against C-N coupling, and whether I am too sceptical of the first.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My own work on nucleotide metabolism and DNA replication does not overlap with any shortlisted candidate, and I have no recorded collaboration with any credited person. I use LC-MS/MS quantification, which is a mild affinity for the proteomics candidate B034, and my biomedical orientation may favour clinically relevant modalities such as B008. I disclose both. Neither is a recusal issue. I have no connection to Crews, Deshaies or Handa.
